title: Sales enablement playbook: positioning, competitive briefs, pitch decks, pricing guidance, case studies, and security FAQ
author: Evelyn Park
content:
Overview

Purpose: This playbook collects Redwood Inference's recommended positioning and messaging, competitive brief templates, pitch deck outlines, pricing guidance & examples, customer case studies, and a prospect-facing security FAQ. Intended users: AE/SDR teams, solutions engineers, sales enablement, and marketing.

Use this document to prepare outreach sequences, tailor competitive responses, craft deal-level pricing, and answer common security questions during RFP and discovery.

Table of contents
1) Elevator pitch and positioning summary
2) Messaging pillars and proof points
3) Competitive brief template + matrix (example competitors: Major Cloud AI, ModelHub, InferenceCo)
4) Pitch deck outline (slide-by-slide recommended content)
5) Pricing guidance and worked examples (hosted, dedicated, private)
6) Two customer case studies with metrics and ROI math
7) Security & compliance FAQ for prospects
8) Deal readiness checklist and recommended collateral

1) Elevator pitch and positioning summary
- Short (1 sentence): Redwood Inference is a developer-first inference platform that delivers predictable, low-latency, and cost-efficient LLM serving across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments with enterprise-grade observability and SLA-backed reliability.
- Medium (30-60s): For engineering and ML teams shipping LLM features, Redwood removes the operational risk and variable cost of model serving by combining a GPU-optimized runtime, automated batching & caching, and a unified control plane across Hosted API, Dedicated capacity, and Private deployments. Customers see 2-5x improvements in cost-per-token and consistent p99 latency SLAs versus ad-hoc self-hosting or generic cloud endpoints.
- Positioning statement: Redwood competes on production economics and developer velocity - reducing inference unit cost, lowering operational overhead, and providing a single interface for devs and platform teams across environments.

2) Messaging pillars and proof points
- Production-grade performance
  - Proof points: GPU-optimized serving runtime, attention kernel selection, continuous batching; internal benchmarks: 30-80% reduced p50 token latency compared to vanilla endpoints on identical hardware (link: /confluence/eng-serving-runtime/benchmarking-and-perf-suite-2025).
  - Customer quote: "We cut inference costs by 40% while improving worst-case latency." - Beta customer (Finance SaaS).
- Cost-aware controls
  - Proof points: per-route batching, KV/prefix caching, quantization recommendations; Redwood Optimize provides suggested profiles that reduce token compute by ~35% on retrieval-augmented workloads.
- Unified deployment modes
  - Proof points: same SDK and rollout primitives across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private; customers can start on Hosted and migrate to Dedicated without code changes.
- Observability & operational controls
  - Proof points: token-level billing, per-model latency breakdowns, canary rollouts, automatic fallback policies; integrated tracing and eval-based regression alerts.

3) Competitive brief template + matrix
- How to use: copy this template into your deal notes and customize with the prospect's priorities (latency, budget, compliance, control).
- Template fields (fill per-competitor): competitor name, typical strengths, common weaknesses, win themes for Redwood, standard objections, rebuttals, evidence/artifacts (benchmarks, case studies, security docs).

Example high-level matrix (use in customer-facing battle cards)
| Criterion | Redwood Inference | MajorCloudAI | ModelHub | InferenceCo |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Time to first API request | < 2 min (hosted) | < 1 min | < 5 min | 2-10 min |
| p99 latency (text generation) | 80-250 ms (varies by model & infra) | 100-350 ms | 120-400 ms | 90-500 ms |
| Cost controls (batching/caching) | Advanced (autotune + suggestions) | Basic | Limited | Plugin-based |
| Dedicated & Private support | Dedicated + VPC/on-prem full support | Dedicated (cloud-only) | Limited | Private via partner |
| Observability & SLOs | Token-level cost + tracing + rollouts | Metrics only | Logs only | Metrics + alerts |
| Enterprise security posture | SOC2, audit logging, KMS integrations | SOC2 subset | Varies | Limited |

Win themes (short bullets you can use in email/objections)
- If a prospect cares about predictable unit economics: emphasize Redwood Optimize, batching, and dedicated pools.
- If a prospect cares about compliance: emphasize Private deployments, KMS/HSM integrations and audit logging.
- If they already self-host: emphasize dev velocity (skip ops), predictable upgrades, and regression alerts tied to evals.

4) Pitch deck outline (recommended 12-15 slide flow)
1. Title & value prop - one-line elevator pitch + customer logo strip.
2. The problem - high-level friction for teams: cost variability, latency surprises, fragile rollouts.
3. Market opportunity - LLM adoption trends, developer-first motion.
4. Redwood solution overview - product modes (Hosted, Dedicated, Private) + one-liner of unique differentiation.
5. How it works (technical) - serving runtime, kernel selection, batching & caching (diagram).
6. Performance evidence - benchmark snapshots, p50/p95/p99 numbers, cost-per-token improvements.
7. Reliability & SLA - dedicated pools, failover policies, SLO examples (p99 latency target, 99.95% uptime).
8. Security & compliance - SOC2, audit logs, KMS, private deployment architecture.
9. Pricing overview - hosted unit pricing, reserved (Dedicated) commitments, private licensing model.
10. ROI example - short worked example for conversational assistant (savings + TCO).
11. Case studies - 1-2 brief customer stories (metrics first).
12. Implementation plan & timeline - PoC -> Pilot -> Production (weeks).
13. Pricing & next steps - recommended pilot offer and who to contact.
14. Appendix - perf details, API examples, FAQ.

Slide notes: include links to collateral for each slide (benchmarks, security pack, case-study PDFs). Keep the deck 12-15 slides for initial meetings; deeper technical sessions use the engineering appendix slides.

5) Pricing guidance and worked examples
- Pricing model primitives
  - Hosted API: pay-as-you-go per token for generations; embeddings priced per embedding unit. Typical published rates: model-dependent (reference published ratecard).
  - Dedicated: reserved GPU pools (monthly/annual commit) + metered overage for bursting. Committed throughput guarantees and lower per-token compute rate.
  - Private: platform fee + optional annual support; on-prem licensing for air-gapped customers.
- Commercial levers to use in negotiation
  - Term length (12/24/36 months) -> discount tiers.
  - Committed throughput (tokens/sec or GPU hours) -> unit price reduction.
  - Feature bundles (extended retention, premium SLAs, advanced observability) -> add-on pricing.
- Worked example: Conversational assistant pilot
  - Assumptions: 5M tokens/month, p50 latency target 250 ms, start on Hosted for 3 months pilot then Dedicated.
  - Hosted estimate: 5M tokens * $0.0005/token = $2,500/month (example list price)
  - Dedicated transition: 1x A10s-equivalent pool reserved = $Xk/month committed -> effective per-token cost falls to $0.00015/token; 5M tokens -> $750/month (after commit and reserved discount).
  - Show customers TCO: factoring infra, ops savings, and downtime reduction typically yields payback in 3-9 months for medium-sized deployments.
- Pricing approval process (internal)
  1. For discounts > 25% or multi-year private deals, submit pricing request to RevOps via the pricing-approval form (link: /confluence/finance-and-legal/contract-templates-2025).
  2. For strategic prospects (>$250k ARR), involve Growth Sales manager and Solutions Engineering for custom TCO modeling.

6) Customer case studies (two short vignettes)
- Case study A: Fintech conversational support (Beta customer)
  - Challenge: slow legacy LLM endpoints increased support latency and produced inconsistent answers.
  - Solution: moved to Redwood Hosted API + prefix caching & batching. Pilot -> production in 4 weeks.
  - Outcomes: 40% reduction in inference costs, p99 latency improved from 1.2s to 220ms, resolution time for automated flows reduced by 28%.
  - Evidence & collateral: internal benchmark report ID: bench-fintech-2025, customer quote, 2-page case PDF (link).
- Case study B: Healthcare enterprise (Private deployment)
  - Challenge: strict data residency and audit requirements required on-prem solution with KMS integration.
  - Solution: Private deployment in VPC with HSM-backed KMS and audit logging; canary rollouts and eval-based regression monitoring.
  - Outcomes: met regulatory controls for pilot audit, improved inference determinism for clinical summaries, estimated 3.2x reduction in engineering ops time spent on inference maintenance.
  - Evidence & collateral: SOC2 evidence package, architecture diagram, implementation guide used.

7) Security & compliance FAQ for prospects (concise answers for initial discovery)
- Q: Which compliance frameworks does Redwood support?
  - A: Redwood maintains SOC 2 Type II attestation, supports contractual requirements for data processing agreements, and provides guidance for GDPR data residency. For higher-assurance requirements we offer Private deployments and audit-support packages.
- Q: How is customer data protected in Hosted mode?
  - A: We use network segmentation between customers, encryption at rest (AES-256), TLS 1.2+ in transit, and per-customer KMS key support for restricted features. Audit logs are available per request.
- Q: Can we run Redwood in our VPC / on-prem?
  - A: Yes. Our Private offering supports VPC-controlled control plane and an on-prem package for air-gapped environments; we integrate with customer KMS/HSM solutions.
- Q: Where are logs and telemetry stored and how long are they retained?
  - A: Default telemetry retention is 90 days; extended retention available as an add-on. Audit logs for enterprise customers can be shipped to customer-owned S3 or SIEM.
- Q: Do you rotate secrets and how are keys managed?
  - A: We support automated key rotation for platform-managed keys and integrations with customer KMS for Bring-Your-Own-Key. Production secrets are stored encrypted and access is RBAC-protected with logged access.
- Q: What is your incident response process and SLA for security incidents?
  - A: We maintain a documented incident response plan, have on-call security staff, and follow NIST-aligned practices. We provide incident notifications per contract and post-incident reports for major events.

8) Deal readiness checklist and recommended collateral
- Deal readiness checklist (copy into CRM opportunity)
  1. Prospect technical fit confirmed (model/mode, latency & throughput requirements).
  2. Security/compliance requirements captured (SOC2, VPC, KMS, data residency).
  3. Expected monthly tokens & spike patterns estimated.
  4. Success metrics & evaluation plan agreed (SLOs, sample prompts, eval criteria).
  5. SE availability for pilot + timeline (2-8 weeks).
  6. Pricing guardrails understood and pricing approval requested if needed.
- Recommended collateral (owners):
  - Quickstart API guide (eng-developer-experience) - owner: Developer Relations.
  - Hosting & Dedicated datasheet (product-docs) - owner: Product Marketing.
  - Security pack (security-and-compliance) - owner: Security.
  - Benchmarks and perf appendix (eng-serving-runtime) - owner: Runtime Eng.
  - Case study PDFs (customer-success-and-support) - owner: Customer Success.

Appendix & where to get help
- For bespoke TCO modeling or large-scale performance validation, contact Solutions Engineering (se-team@redwood.com) and link to internal perf lab (confluence/eng-serving-runtime/benchmarking-and-perf-suite-2025).
- For security questions beyond this FAQ, send prospects to security-pack@redwood.com and include the security pack (link: /confluence/security-and-compliance/audit-logging).
